cells.trigger_snippet: (reflection on 5 cells: cell-0011, cell-0012, cell-0013, cell-0014, cell-0015)
cells.prompt: (reflective loop -- system prompt was reflect.SYSTEM_PROMPT; user content was the recent cells as multimodal input)
cells.caption:
The notebook has two distinct registers running in parallel: cells 0011–0013 are pure infrastructure demos (animated_svg, scene3d, aframe) with no real content, while cells 0014–0015 are two successive attempts to render the same Doña Esperanza milpa snippet — suggesting the image pipeline was run twice, possibly to compare or refine output. The conversation thread has now landed on a specific, human-scale agrarian story: intergenerational seed custody, terraced soil conservation, and the Three Sisters milpa system in highland Oaxaca.

What worked: Cell-0015 is clearly the stronger render: it captures bone-white/cream corn stalks, bean vines climbing the stalks (visible green climbing tendrils), a stone-walled terrace edge, and Doña Esperanza's figure in a rebozo-style wrap with a planting stick — all specific details from the snippet. The rolling hills and winding river below ground the highland geography. The oil-painting treatment gives it ethnographic weight without romanticizing poverty.

What didn't: Cell-0014 partially misses: the corn is rendered chalk-white/skeletal (almost dead-looking) rather than the pale cream of a heritage white maize variety, the beans are absent entirely, and the woman is crouched and faceless rather than recognizable as a custodian. The terracing is architecturally accurate but the scene reads as post-harvest devastation rather than active tending. The village in the background looks Moroccan/Mediterranean rather than Zapotec highland. Cells 0011–0013 are infrastructure noise relative to the content thread.

Proposed next (text): The milpa is not a field — it is a covenant. Corn provides the vertical scaffold; beans fix the nitrogen the corn depletes; squash seals the soil against sun and rain. Each plant is doing work for the others, and Doña Esperanza is doing work for all three: her terraces slow the water, her planting stick opens the soil without inverting it, and her seed selection — choosing the straightest, heaviest ears to replant — is a breeding program running across sixty years of her family's memory.
cells.classifier_reasoning: The two image cells have now established the visual scene. What's missing is the conceptual grounding — the milpa as a mutualistic system, and the human role within it as a form of slow, embodied knowledge. A text cell here would anchor the ecological and intergenerational logic that the images gesture at but can't articulate: why the Three Sisters work, what "tending" actually means as a technical and mnemonic act, and why 1962 is a significant date worth naming (the grandfather's original seed stock predates Green Revolution hybridization pressure in Mexico). This would set up a potential follow-on vega or mermaid cell visualizing the nitrogen cycle or the Three Sisters companion-planting geometry.
